title: A Hollow for the Oath Anew
premise: Felix Okonkwo, exiled for a storm they did not mean to call, has spent seven years keeping the ledgers of the Hollow Guild, brokers of impossible things, hidden in the border city of Vess. When the wards fall and the stars go out on the same night, Felix discovers the guild's founder bargained away the sky itself to buy the city's survival—and that Felix's own exile was engineered to keep them from ever learning it. Hunted by both realms and betrayed within the guild, Felix must gather the scattered oath-keepers of the old covenant and reforge it at the Hollow's heart before the thirteenth moon turns, choosing at last between their own survival and a justice no law will sanction. In the end, Felix pays the ledger's true price—giving up their name and memory of home—to relight the stars, and walks into Vess as a stranger the city owes everything to.
about_author: Beatrix Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial-era trade ledgers before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people who keep accounts—of debts, of oaths, of what survival actually costs.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. During a routine guild audit, the border wards collapse and every star vanishes at once; panic spreads through Vess while Felix alone notices the ledgers recorded the fall three days in advance. The emotional beat is dread—the quiet life Felix built is over, and someone inside knew.

chapters.title: Ledgers of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Interrogating the guild's master broker, Ilsa, Felix learns the founder once traded with something beyond the wards—but Ilsa lies badly, and Felix finds a page torn from the founding covenant bearing their own family seal. The beat is betrayal sharpening into resolve: this was never random.

chapters.title: What Exile Was For
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Felix and a ward-soldier named Captain Rhee who once escorted Felix out of the realm. Rhee arrives not to arrest but to warn: the crown blames storm-callers for the darkened sky, and hunters are coming. The beat is reluctant alliance—two people bound by an old injustice neither can undo alone.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon
chapters.summary: Rhee's POV. An astronomer-priest reveals the covenant's terms: thirteen turns of darkness, then the realm beyond consumes Vess entirely unless the oath is reforged at its origin. The beat is vertigo—the scale of the deadline makes every small loyalty suddenly weight-bearing.

chapters.title: Debts Owed the Hollow
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Using the guild's own debt-ledgers, Felix blackmails and begs scattered oath-keepers out of hiding—a disgraced bridge-witch, a mute bell-founder, a child who remembers the old tongue. The beat is wary hope: power gathered from the desperate is power that can turn.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa, revealed as the founder's daughter, justifies her father's bargain and her own sabotage: the covenant demanded a willing sacrifice each century, and she chose the city over strangers. The beat is chilling sympathy—an antagonist whose math almost works.

chapters.title: Storm Without a Caller
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Hunters corner the company at the drowned bridge; Felix calls a storm deliberately for the first time since exile, saving Rhee but confirming every accusation against them. The beat is grief and self-recognition—the weapon they fled becoming the tool they choose.

chapters.title: The Origin of the Oath
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. At the covenant's birthplace beneath the Hollow, the company learns the original oath was forged by exiles like Felix—people the law discarded—who traded memory itself for protection. The beat is revelation reframing everything: the price was always identity.

chapters.title: A Covenant Reforged
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, climax. On the thirteenth turn, Ilsa offers Felix a loophole—sacrifice the child instead—and Felix refuses, breaking the ledger's logic entirely by offering their name, memories, and exile freely. The stars reignite mid-oath. The beat is costly triumph: justice achieved outside every law, paid in full.

chapters.title: Stranger in a City That Owes You
chapters.summary: Rhee's POV, resolution. Weeks later, Vess rebuilds under a mended sky; Rhee finds Felix working anonymously in a rebuilt guild hall, remembered by no one, owed by everyone. Rhee chooses not to tell them who they were. The beat is bittersweet peace—survival redefined as what we give, not what we keep.
